_readme: Fractional-index keys for order_position (spec 024). A client mints one optimistically
for a mid-list insert so the row renders in the right place before the server's
authoritative position arrives. This is a port of fractional_indexing.py and must
produce the SAME key for the same neighbours, or the optimistic row jumps on settle.
What a port must match exactly:
- Alphabet is base-62 '0-9A-Z a-z' (no space), ordered by byte value. Keys are
ASCII, so byte order, UTF-16 code-unit order and code-point order all agree.
Compare with plain byte/lexicographic order, never a locale-aware compare.
- A shorter key that is a prefix of a longer one sorts FIRST ('V' < 'V0').
- null and '' mean the same thing: no neighbour on that side.
- generateBetween with before >= after does NOT throw here: it falls back to
generateAppend(before). The Python raises ValueError instead. The client
behaviour is the one to copy.
Known quirk, shared with the Python: a neighbour key ending in '0' has no key
strictly below it with the same prefix, so generateBetween(null, '0') returns '0V',
which sorts AFTER '0'. Neither implementation ever mints a key ending in '0', so
this only bites on hand-written positions. The cases below pin it (see their notes)
so a port reproduces it rather than 'fixing' one side.

cases.name: Z rolls into the lowercase block
z extends with the midpoint char
trailing z extends a longer key
no before, 1 -> 0V (no room at this level)
no before, 0V -> recurse into the tail
no before, 0 -> 0V
cases.note: Quirk shared with the Python: '0V' sorts AFTER '0'. There is no key below '0'; unreachable from minted keys.

cases.name: no before, 00 -> 00V
cases.note: Same trailing-'0' quirk: the result sorts after 'after'.

cases.name: wide gap takes the floor midpoint
adjacent chars extend before with V
longer before, adjacent at first diff
after is longer, not a prefix
before is a prefix of after: halve the suffix
prefix, suffix 0 -> 0V
cases.note: Trailing-'0' quirk: 'A0V' sorts after 'A0'. Nothing exists strictly between 'A' and 'A0'.

cases.name: before == after falls back to append (the Python raises)
before > after falls back to append (the Python raises)
